A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SSLA/SSLA-Det work, with readable text, equations, figures and tables supporting reliable matching. Both end with references; neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original SSLA-Det experiments on Gen1 and N-Caltech101, training and inference measurements, ablations and detection examples.

after.justification: Section 4 retains the original detection, timing and ablation results and adds a component-level efficiency-attribution experiment.

M1.justification: Section 3.4 revises the specified architecture: pooling and temporal dropout change from every stage to the first three stages, and 1x1 conversion changes from YOLOX's stem to all head convolutions. The core MOS, PAP and scatter-compute-gather procedure remains unchanged. These reported revisions do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: Both versions train and evaluate on Gen1 automotive detection and N-Caltech101 detection. The added efficiency study uses existing Gen1 validation coverage without introducing another dataset, task or input scenario.

E2.justification: The benchmark comparator sets in Tables 1–2 and the LSTM comparison remain unchanged. New Table 5 introduces a dense-activation comparator retaining MOS and PAP, alongside temporal-dropout and sparse-pooling removal controls.

E3.justification: New Table 5 adds a controlled evaluation design on Gen1 validation, including comparison of sparse and dense activation with temporal dropout disabled and MOS/PAP retained. Existing training budgets, augmentation, metrics and timing procedures remain as stated.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 adds a focused efficiency-attribution study separating the contributions of sparse activation, temporal dropout and sparse pooling. Existing spatial-sparsity, PAP and patch-size ablations remain, with old Tables 5–7 becoming Tables 6–8. Figure 4's failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added ablation uses the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1, 2 and 4 retain their scores and latency values. Table 3 changes SSLA-S mAP from 0.335 to 0.334 and SSLA-B parameters from 0.868M to 0.902M. Old Table 5/new Table 6 changes SSLA-S mAP from 0.355 to 0.335. New Table 5 reports component-removal results, including 1.02 versus 388 MFLOPS/event at 0.370 mAP with temporal dropout disabled.

T1.justification: The causal formulation, mathematical definitions, Equations (1)–(8) and per-event complexity statement remain substantively unchanged. No theorem, proof or new mathematical derivation is introduced; Algorithm 1's indexing correction concerns pseudocode consistency.

C1.justification: Both versions claim spatially sparse, parallel-trainable linear attention, the first end-to-end asynchronous linear-attention detector, and leading asynchronous accuracy with over 20-fold lower computation. The headline 0.375 Gen1 and 0.515 N-Caltech101 mAP claims are retained.

C2.justification: The earlier recurrence/temporal-dropout explanation of efficiency is removed, while new Section 4.4 emphasizes sparse activation's dominant contribution under its controls. Section 5 replaces the explicit hardware-limited scaling discussion with an accuracy–latency trade-off argument that rejects interpreting the accuracy gap as a methodological shortcoming. The FARSE-CNN analogy and PAP translation-invariance interpretation are also removed.

D1.justification: The abstract newly states code availability and supplies a repository link. Algorithm 1 corrects event slices from [Ai:A(i+1)] to [A(i-1):Ai], aligning them with the stated event indexing. Most software, hardware and training hyperparameter disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds State Space Models for Event Cameras and replaces Graves's LSTM reference with Hochreiter and Schmidhuber's original work. It emphasizes spatially structured routing and PAP when distinguishing SSLA from memory-routing approaches, while removing the FARSE-CNN analogy. Most cited research remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and method explanations receive wording refinements, several subsection headings are renamed, and the discussion is rewritten. v2 also expands affiliations and adds keywords, corresponding-author information and acknowledgements. The overall section sequence and most technical prose remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The document changes from two columns to a single-column layout with running headers and redistributed tables. Figures 2 and 3 are substantially redrawn to explain state decomposition, parallel training and architecture. A new efficiency table is added, and table headings and units are refined. Figures 1 and 4 retain their content but are resized.

improvement.justification: New Table 5 provides better controlled support for efficiency attribution, Figures 2–3 explain the mechanism more clearly, and reporting corrections, consistent pseudocode indexing and code-access information improve checkability. These gains are tempered by Section 5 removing the explicit untested-scaling limitation and making a stronger claim that the accuracy gap is not methodological. Overall, the evidence supports a limited net improvement.
